name: Ara
title: Descendant of Asher through Jether
summary: Ara is a biblical figure known exclusively from the genealogy of the tribe of Asher in 1 Chronicles. He is listed as the son of Jether in 1 Chron 7:38, along with his brothers Jeftunne and Pispa. Beyond this brief mention, Ara has no independent narrative role in Scripture. The genealogies in the books of Chronicles served a vital function for the Israelite community, especially during the period after the exile in Babylon: they confirmed the tribes' historical roots, secured inheritance rights, and anchored the identity of the returned people. That even lesser-known names like Ara were carefully preserved in these lists testifies to a fundamental conviction that every member of God's people has value and a place in the greater story of salvation.

versions.summary: Ara is a figure who appears in the genealogies in 1 Chronicles, where he is listed as the son of Jether within the tribe of Asher. His name occurs only in 1 Chr 7:38, and he plays no independent role in the biblical narrative beyond his place in the genealogy. The family lists in the books of Chronicles served an important function for Israel's self-understanding, especially after the return from Babylon, when the ancestral lines of the tribes were carefully documented to ensure continuity, belonging, and inheritance rights. Ara thus represents the broader theological value that every single name among God's people was considered worthy of preservation.

footnotes.text: The name Ara (Hebrew: אֲרָא) can mean "wild goat" or "traveler." The name occurs only in 1 Chr 7:38 and is a hapax legomenon – that is, a word or name that appears only once in the Hebrew Bible text.

The genealogies in 1 Chronicles were likely compiled and edited during the Persian period to restore and document the origins of the tribes and legitimize the people's identity after returning from the Babylonian exile. Even seemingly peripheral names held great value for preserving tribal continuity and inheritance rights.

The tribe of Asher was allotted its territory in northwestern Canaan along the Mediterranean coast (Josh 19:24–31). The genealogical list in 1 Chr 7:30–40 is more detailed than parallel sources, suggesting that the Chronicler may have used his own independent tribal lists.

In 1 Chr 7:38, Jether is mentioned as the father of Ara, Jephunneh, and Pispa. Some scholars have debated whether this is the same Jether mentioned in verse 37 (also called Jithran), making the exact lineage somewhat disputed.
